frozen_problem.title: Tate-completion obstruction and finite torsion windows for the motivic filtration on TC of the sphere
frozen_problem.statement:
The motivic filtration on the algebraic $K$-theory of the sphere spectrum

Due to work of Rognes, Blumberg--Mandell, and others, we understand the algebraic K-theory of the sphere spectrum fairly well. Recent work of Hahn--Raksit--Wilson \cite{arXiv:2206.11208} gives a motivic filtration on TC of $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-rings which is closely related to the motivic filtration on algebraic K-theory in motivic homotopy theory.

Can one understand the motivic filtration (or motivic spectral sequence) on the $\mathrm{TC}$ of the sphere spectrum? What about for the motivic filtration on related invariants such as $\mathrm{THH}$, $\mathrm{TP}$?

theory.target: Determine how nearest-neighbour additive extension data changes the exponent despite identical associated graded, and whether bounded graded exponent plus complete separated filtration forces rational vanishing.
definitions: For prime p and e in {0,1}^{n-1}, G has generators x_i with p*x_i=e_i*x_(i+1), p*x_(n-1)=0.
Digit truncation defines the inverse system; F^s consists of sequences with initial s digits zero.
Blocks are maximal intervals joined by1-edges; a block length counts digits, not carry edges.
A(e) uses one fixed infinite edge sequence, and rationalization is Q tensor_Z A(e).
The filtered cochain model is concentrated in degree zero; homological amplitude and filtration width are distinct.
assumptions: p is prime. At length n the abelian presentation has p*x_i=e_i*x_(i+1), e_i in {0,1}, for i<n-1, and p*x_(n-1)=0.
Transition maps discard the last digit; filtration is by vanishing initial digits, not necessarily p-adic powers.
The infinite model uses a single fixed edge sequence and its compatible truncations.
All-degree and infinite-limit arguments remain ordinary unverified proof obligations; finite results do not prove them.
No identification with TC, Tate, a motivic filtration or a cyclotomic Frobenius is asserted.
approaches_considered: Cut at zero edges and eliminate block relations; derive exact orders and the infinite product/limit criterion.
Normalize literal digit sums and repeatedly add to zero; check explicit maps without the block formula.
Retire edge-count and collapsed-page-only shortcuts; audit which filtration property rationalization destroys.
falsification_targets: Number of nonzero carries determines exponent.
Identical complete convergent collapsed pages determine the rationalized abutment.
Surjectivity alone certifies the proposed finite-group isomorphism.

claims.statement: For a fixed prime and digit length, the number of nonzero nearest-neighbour carry edges determines the exponent. Refuted at p=2,n=4 by words 110 and101: exponents8 and4 despite four identical graded layers and two carry edges.
claims.falsification_condition: A failed presentation isomorphism, wrong witness order, different graded layer or mismatched number of edges.

claims.statement: For every prime p and finite binary edge word, block lengths L_j give G=product Z/p^(L_j), exponent p^(max L_j), and p^(sum min(k,L_j)) elements killed by p^k for k>=0.
claims.falsification_condition: An incorrect normal form, relation elimination, or block isomorphism outside the finite checked domain.

claims.statement: For every fixed infinite binary edge sequence in this presentation family, Q tensor A(e)=0 iff the digit-block lengths are uniformly bounded. Identical convergent collapsed pages for the all-carry and zero-carry degree-zero complexes do not determine rationalized abutments.
claims.falsification_condition: A failure of product/limit identification, absence of a claimed infinite-order element, wrong convergence convention, or failure of separation/completeness of the integral filtration.

claims.statement: A filtration of length L with all layers killed by p has total group killed by p^L; this exponent is sharp. Bounded homological amplitude alone does not impose finite filtration width.
claims.falsification_condition: A failed inclusion p F^i subset F^(i+1), indexing error, or failure of the stated all-carry sharpness witness.

claims.statement: Stacks012K Definition12.24.9 specifies convergence through the graded abutment and filtration conditions; Lemma12.24.11 assumes finite termwise filtrations. Stacks00CM gives the single-annihilator localization relation. Neither supplies a calculation of TC here.
claims.falsification_condition: A wrong source locator, changed hypothesis, or confusion between finite filtration and homological amplitude.

progress.summary: Four identical graded layers and two carry edges conceal exponents8 versus4; exact isomorphism matrices and surviving multiples certify the distinction.

The derived infinite family isolates missing extension data and loss of separatedness after rationalization, with a bounded-block criterion and sharp finite-width repair pending independent proof review.
